_about: Starquake inputs for app/starquake.js. numax/dnu in microhertz. 'published_*' are literature values; 'numax'/'dnu' on Kepler stars are measured from the light curve by pipeline/starquake.py. M, R in solar units, teff in K. Values marked approximate are rounded literature values used only for predictions.

sun.name: The Sun
sun.ref: Solar reference values: Kjeldsen & Bedding 1995, A&A 293, 87; Huber et al. 2011, ApJ 743, 143
sun.note: Stanford's SoSH project played the Sun's real Doppler data this way: a hum near 126 Hz with slow beats about 5.7 Hz apart.

hip87937.name: Barnard's Star
hip87937.note: Red dwarfs are predicted to have tiny, very fast starquakes, but none has been detected yet: this is a prediction.

wanderers_eps_indi_b.name: Epsilon Indi B
wanderers_eps_indi_b.params_ref: approximate (brown dwarf pair; masses ~0.05-0.07 solar masses)
wanderers_eps_indi_b.note: Brown dwarfs are predicted to oscillate, but it has never been detected: this is a prediction only.

wanderers_wise0855.name: WISE 0855-0714
wanderers_wise0855.params_ref: approximate (3-10 Jupiter masses, about Jupiter's size)
wanderers_wise0855.note: This is a sub-stellar object colder than the North Pole; any starquakes are purely theoretical. Prediction only.

wanderers_rw_aur.name: RW Aurigae
wanderers_rw_aur.note: RW Aur's dimming comes from dust and accretion, not starquakes; solar-like oscillations are only predicted here.

wanderers_r_dra.name: R Draconis
wanderers_r_dra.note: R Dra's 245-day Mira pulsation is a different, self-driven kind of pulsation. The starquake model is a prediction only, and needs a large extra speed-up to be heard.

hip11767.name: Polaris
hip11767.note: Polaris is a Cepheid: its 4-day pulsation is a different, self-driven kind. Solar-like starquakes are only predicted here.
